recommendation: Keep this commit as-is. It completes the FHIR-20400 textual reconciliation without narrowing later-approved regex behavior; follow-up is only needed if the work group separately decides to change the 1-to-9 digit fractional-second policy.
issue_request: FHIR-20400 was Published/Persuasive for FHIR-core datatypes. It reported that the time prose only described hh:mm:ss even though the regex allowed fractional seconds, and the resolution said to update time and dateTime text to allow milliseconds.
initial_application: Historical commit 0ed3302de365979d3eee6f8c96cd9570acb542d8 changed the old inline time regex from unbounded fractional digits to a 1-to-3 digit pattern, but did not update all current prose/primitive-definition surfaces. A separate earlier batch had added dateTime millisecond wording, but later regex refactoring and decisions left the active primitive regexes at 1-to-9 fractional digits.
additional_context: The active datatype page renders regexes from source/datatypes/primitives.xml via [%regex ...%] placeholders. Later dateTime decisions FHIR-38735 and FHIR-52878 retained optional 1-to-9 fractional seconds, and FHIR-42984 separately clarified sub-millisecond precision for instant. The Jira-linked Zulip thread records that fractions were intended and that up to 9 digits were supported.
reconciliation: Updated source/datatypes.html and source/datatypes/primitives.xml so dateTime and time both state that fractional seconds are optionally allowed. The regexes were intentionally left unchanged because later final decisions already define the current 1-to-9 digit fractional precision behavior.
source_changes: source/datatypes.html: dateTime prose now says fractional seconds are optionally allowed; time prose now describes hh:mm:ss with optional fractional seconds.
source/datatypes/primitives.xml: dateTime and time primitive definition text now acknowledges optional fractional seconds; regexes were unchanged.
